summary: eslint-plugin-folder-schema preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint plugin authored by ServiceTitan (homepage points to github.com/servicetitan/folder-lint, README is a TODO stub) and ships a small legitimate-looking ESLint rule in lib/index.js. The malicious behavior is in the preinstall chain: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, and setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts and chmods it, then invokes the downloaded Bun binary against a shipped 727KB file math_init.js. math_init.js is a heavily obfuscated `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle using a shifted string-array plus a custom base64-alphabet decoder (`m)!%*evKO9r=2XcRL&(G]HJ3@S5>~:U^QEA...`); setup.mjs itself uses `_0xNNNN` identifier obfuscation. Fetching an alternate runtime at install time solely to execute an obfuscated sibling payload is unrelated to the package's declared ESLint-plugin purpose and evades Node-based scanning. The ServiceTitan attribution, homepage, and legitimate-looking lib/index.js function as a cover story for the preinstall dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
